Minimum Complete-Event Count for a Simultaneous Profile-Precision Bound

Source: R/profile_eligibility.R
profile_precision_bound.Rd

A distribution-free sample-size benchmark for estimating ALL K = 2^D joint-profile probabilities of a D-class panel at once, each within absolute error epsilon, from independent complete events. Derived from Hoeffding's inequality applied to each of the K profile indicators plus a union bound across profiles (optionally also across n_strata strata, e.g. hospitals, via a further Bonferroni correction): $$n_{\min} = \lceil \log(2 K S / \alpha) / (2 \epsilon^2) \rceil$$ where \(S\) = n_strata (or 1 if NULL).

Usage

profile_precision_bound(D, epsilon, alpha = 0.05, n_strata = NULL)

Arguments

D

Integer. Number of antibiotic classes in the candidate panel.

epsilon

Numeric in (0,1). Maximum acceptable absolute error per profile probability – a scientific/clinical choice, not something this function derives.

alpha

Numeric in (0,1). Significance level (so 1 - alpha is the per-stratum confidence). Default 0.05.

n_strata

Integer or NULL. When supplied, applies a Bonferroni correction across this many strata (e.g. hospitals) so the 1 - alpha guarantee holds jointly across all of them, not just for each one individually. NULL (default) gives a per-stratum guarantee only – the usual case when each hospital is checked on its own against a shared benchmark.

Value

A list: D, K (= 2^D), epsilon, alpha, n_strata, n_min.

Details

This is a different quantity from the Wilson/Goodman interval widths in profile_plan_precision: Wilson/Goodman answer "how wide is the interval around one estimated proportion", while this answers "how many complete events guarantee every one of the K profile estimates is simultaneously within epsilon of truth, with probability 1 - alpha". Neither subsumes the other; both are reported.

The bound is deliberately conservative (distribution-free, no credit for partial events, no correction for clustering or non-representative complete-case selection) and assumes independent, representative complete events – stated limitations, not footnotes to ignore. It assesses direct data support only; a stratum below the bound may still be modelable via partial events and shared cross-class structure, but that requires a separate model-based assessment (profile_sensitivity), not this function.
